questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay titled“Is technology making people lazy?”.The statement given below is for your reference. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words . Many studies claim that computers distract people, make them lazy thinkers and even lower their work efficiency.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Is technology making people lazy? My answer is a qualified yes: while technology itself is neutral, the way most of us use it does breed laziness of both mind and body.

To begin with, technology encourages mental laziness. When a search engine can answer any question in seconds and a navigation app can guide every turn, few people bother to think, memorize or reason on their own. Gradually, we outsource our brains and lose the habit of deep thinking. Physical laziness follows the same logic: with delivery apps and online services, many people rarely walk, cook or move, so their bodies grow as idle as their minds.

Admittedly, technology can also make us more efficient. Yet the tool is not to blame; our passive dependence is. Therefore, the real question is not whether technology makes us lazy, but whether we control it or let it control us. Used wisely, it frees us; used blindly, it enslaves us.

transcript.text: An 81-year-old man ended up in Germany by accident after trying to get from Newcastle, Great Britain, to Rome, Italy.
transcript.zh: 一位81岁的老人在试图从英国纽卡斯尔前往意大利罗马时意外到达了德国。

transcript.text: The old age pensioner was on a mission to see the Pope, who is head of the Catholic Church, and decided to make his way there by car.
transcript.zh: 这位领取养老金的老人此行是为了拜见天主教会领袖教皇,他决定驾车前往。

transcript.text: He was surprised when his GPS system told him he had arrived, although there were no signs of any of the famous buildings or architecture.
transcript.zh: 当GPS系统告诉他已经到达目的地时,他感到很惊讶,因为周围没有任何著名建筑的迹象。

transcript.text: The man parked but didn't put on the handbrake of his car properly.
transcript.zh: 老人停好车,但没有正确拉上手刹。

transcript.text: His car rolled backwards, and in a striking display of irony, hit a sign saying "Rom"—the small town in North Germany he had mistakenly plugged into the GPS system.
transcript.zh: 他的车向后滑行,极具讽刺意味的是,撞上了一块写着"Rom"的标志牌——这是他误输入GPS系统的德国北部小镇的名字。

transcript.text: Police said that the car had come to a halt after hitting the sign, but did not appear to be seriously damaged, although an ambulance was called to check on the pensioner.
transcript.zh: 警方表示,汽车撞上标志牌后停了下来,但似乎没有严重损坏,不过还是叫了救护车来检查这位老人的身体状况。

transcript.text: The man, who lives in the UK and is originally Italian, might have been confused by the fact that Rome is written "Roma" in Italian and "Rom" in German.
transcript.zh: 这位生活在英国、原籍意大利的老人可能是因为罗马在意大利语中写作"Roma",而在德语中写作"Rom"而产生了混淆。

questions.stem: What did the old age pensioner plan to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The old age pensioner was on a mission to see the Pope, who is head of the Catholic Church, and decided to make his way there by car.信号：表目的的 on a mission to + decided to 。答案信号是表 "目的 / 决意" 的措辞：on a mission to see the Pope（肩负见教皇的使命）和 decided to m…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音里 trying to get from Newcastle 确实念到了 Newcastle，但那是他的 "出发地"，不是要 "go to" 的目的地。选项 Go to Newcastle. 盗用这个原词，把起点说成终点，听到 Newcastle 就选必中招。 借用原文：ended up in Germany by accident
optionAnalysis.C: 答非所问：Germany 是他 "误打误撞最后到达" 的地方（ended up in Germany by accident），并非他 "打算" 去的地方。选项 Travel to Germany. 把 "意外结果" 安到 "计划" 头上，正是本题问 plan 时最阴的干扰。 借用原文：on a mission to see the Pope
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：罗马（Italian city）虽是他的真正目的地，但 Tour an Italian city. 把目的说成 "游览一座意大利城市"，与录音 on a mission to see the Pope（去见教皇）这一明确目的不符——他不是去观光，是去见教皇。选项借意大利城市这层背景来诱选。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（on a mission to see the Pope ↔ See the Pope. 去修饰语后核心动作不变）

questions.evidenceText: The old age pensioner was on a mission to see the Pope, who is head of the Catholic Church, and decided to make his way there by car.

questions.stem: What finally happened to the old man?

options.text: He was taken to hospital in an ambulance.
His car hit a sign and was badly damaged.
His GPS system went out of order.
He ended up in the wrong place.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：An 81-year-old man ended up in Germany by accident after trying to get from Newcastle, Great Britain, to Rome, Italy.信号：结果词 ended up + by accident 。答案信号是表 "最终结果" 的措辞 ended up in Germany by accident：ended up（最终落到…）+ by accident（出…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音 an ambulance was called to check on the pensioner 是 "叫了救护车来查看"，并没说把他送进医院。选项 He was taken to hospital in an ambulance. 盗用 ambulance 这个原词，再加码成 "被送往医院"，听到 ambulance 就选必错。 借用原文：did not appear to be seriously damaged
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：车确实 hit a sign（撞了路牌），但录音明说 did not appear to be seriously damaged（看起来没严重损坏）。选项 His car hit a sign and was badly damaged. 前半句盗用原词为真、后半 badly damaged 与原文相反，是典型 "半真半假" 陷阱。 借用原文：his GPS system told him he had arrived
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：录音里 GPS 一直正常工作（his GPS system told him he had arrived），错的是老人把目的地 "Rom" 输错了，不是 GPS 坏了。选项 His GPS system went out of order. 盗用 GPS 这个高频原词，硬安一个 "故障" 给它，把人为输错说成机器失灵。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（ended up in Germany by accident ↔ He ended up in the wrong place. 具体地名概括成 wrong place）

transcript.text: Glasgow has pledged to become the first carbon neutral city in the UK. The city's council and ScottishPower have announced a range of strategies in an attempt to reduce carbon emissions ahead of the new national target of 2045.
transcript.zh: Glasgow承诺成为英国首个碳中和城市。该市议会和ScottishPower宣布了一系列战略，试图在2045年这一新的国家目标之前减少碳排放。

transcript.text: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon welcomed the pledge, and said: "Today's announcement between ScottishPower and Glasgow City Council—to make Glasgow the UK's first net-zero city—is a very welcome step. Reaching our goals will need exactly this kind of partnership approach—with government, business, local authorities and citizens all playing their part."
transcript.zh: 首席大臣Nicola Sturgeon对这一承诺表示欢迎，并说："今天ScottishPower与Glasgow市议会之间的宣布——使Glasgow成为英国首个净零排放城市——是非常值得欢迎的一步。实现我们的目标需要正是这种伙伴关系方式——政府、企业、地方当局和公民都发挥各自的作用。"

transcript.text: Speaking ahead of the All Energy Conference being held in Glasgow, ScottishPower chief executive Keith Anderson said: "We have a large supply of renewable energy on our doorstep and one of the only two low emission zones in action across the UK. Now, we need to invest in the technologies and programmes that transform the rest of Glasgow's economy and make us net zero before anyone else."
transcript.zh: 在Glasgow举行的全能源大会之前发言时, ScottishPower首席执行官Keith Anderson说："我们家门口有大量的可再生能源供应，并且拥有全英国仅有的两个低排放区之一。现在，我们需要投资于技术和项目，以转变Glasgow经济的其他部分，使我们比其他任何人都更早实现净零排放。"

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report?

options.text: Scotland will reach the national target in carbon emissions reduction ahead of schedule.
Glasgow City Council has made a deal with ScottishPower on carbon emissions.
Glasgow has pledged to take the lead in reducing carbon emissions in the UK.
First Minister Nicola Sturgeon urged ScottishPower to reduce carbon emissions.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：Glasgow has pledged to become the first carbon neutral city in the UK.信号：新闻首句即点题 。信号是「新闻第一句」：英文短消息几乎都把最重要的事放在开头第一句。Glasgow has pledged to become the first carbon neutral city in the…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 盗用了录音 the new national target of 2045 里的 national target 一词，编出「苏格兰将提前达成全国减排目标」。但录音只说格拉斯哥要「赶在 2045 全国目标之前（ahead of）」实现零碳，是这一座城市立下承诺，并非「苏格兰整体将提前达标」，属听到 target 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：The city's council and ScottishPower have announced a range of strategies
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：B 盗用了录音多次出现的 ScottishPower 和 Glasgow City Council，说成「市议会与 ScottishPower 就碳排放达成一桩交易」。录音里二者确有合作（announced a range of strategies），但新闻主旨是「格拉斯哥承诺成为英国首个零碳城市」这件大事，B 把主旨缩成一个次要的「达成 deal」细节，以偏概全。 借用原文：First Minister Nicola Sturgeon welcomed the pledge
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 盗用了录音里的 First Minister Nicola Sturgeon 和 ScottishPower 两个专名，编成「Sturgeon 敦促 ScottishPower 减排」。但录音里 Sturgeon 是 welcomed the pledge（对承诺表示欢迎），并没有「敦促」ScottishPower，方向与事实都不符，是把人名拼凑成假信息的张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（pledged to become the first carbon neutral city in the UK ↔ pledged to take the lead in reducing carbon emissions in the UK 「第一个碳中和」=「带头减排」）

questions.evidenceText: Glasgow has pledged to become the first carbon neutral city in the UK.

questions.stem: What did ScottishPower's chief executive say ahead of the All Energy Conference?

options.text: Glasgow needs to invest in new technologies to reach its goal.
Glasgow is going to explore new sources of renewable energy.
Stricter regulation is needed in transforming Glasgow's economy.
It's necessary to create more low-emission zones as soon as possible.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Now, we need to invest in the technologies and programmes that transform the rest of Glasgow's economy and make us net zero before anyone else.信号：主张句 we need to… 是落点 。信号是说话人亲口的主张句 we need to invest in the technologies and programmes：题问「他说了什么」，答案就在他原话里 we…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 盗用了录音 a large supply of renewable energy 里的 renewable energy。但说话人说的是「我们已经拥有大量可再生能源」，是现状陈述，并非主张「去探索新的可再生能源来源（explore new sources）」。听到 renewable energy 就选 B 正中圈套。 借用原文：one of the only two low emission zones in action across the UK
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 说「改造格拉斯哥经济需要更严格的监管（Stricter regulation）」。录音里说话人主张的是 invest in the technologies and programmes（投资技术与项目），从头到尾没提 regulation 或加强监管，C 属录音根本没说的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 盗用了录音 one of the only two low emission zones in action 里的 low emission zones。但说话人是把「已经在运行的低排放区」当作格拉斯哥的现有优势来陈述，并没有主张「有必要尽快多建低排放区（create more … as soon as possible）」，是把现状包装成主张的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（we need to invest in the technologies and programmes ↔ Glasgow needs to invest in new technologies to reach its goal 「投资于技术」原意保留，仅换措辞）

questions.evidenceText: Now, we need to invest in the technologies and programmes that transform the rest of Glasgow's economy and make us net zero before anyone else.

transcript.text: A Japanese IT firm has officially introduced an "office cat" policy to combat the stressful environment of the workplace.
transcript.zh: 一家日本IT公司正式推出了"办公室猫"政策,以应对压力重重的工作环境。

transcript.text: A total of nine furry friends freely wander around in the office and do whatever their little hearts desire.
transcript.zh: 共有九只毛茸茸的朋友在办公室里自由走动,做着它们内心想做的任何事情。

transcript.text: Hidenobu Fukuda, who heads the firm, introduced the pet policy, upon request from one of his employees, allowing staff to bring their own cats to work.
transcript.zh: 公司负责人Hidenobu Fukuda应一位员工的要求推出了这项宠物政策,允许员工将自己的猫带到工作场所。

transcript.text: Employee Eri Ito is grateful for their animals' comforting ways. "Cats are sleeping just beside us. It's healing." she said. Not only does Fukuda encourage bringing cats to the job, but he also encourages his employees to rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets. He gives 5,000 yen, about 45 US dollars a month to those who rescue a cat.
transcript.zh: 员工Eri Ito对这些动物带来的慰藉心怀感激。她说:"猫就睡在我们身边,这很治愈。"Fukuda不仅鼓励员工带猫上班,还鼓励员工从过度拥挤的收容所或街头救助猫。他每月向救助猫的员工提供5000日元,约合45美元。

transcript.text: While the positives are many, there are still some obstacles. "Sometimes a cat will walk on a phone and cut off the call, or they shut down the computers by walking onto the off switch," Ito says.
transcript.zh: 虽然好处很多,但仍存在一些障碍。Ito说:"有时猫会走到电话上挂断通话,或者它们走到关机开关上把电脑关掉。"

transcript.text: Still, cats in the workplace have been a tremendous success for the company. The policy has led to various other companies doing the same.
transcript.zh: 尽管如此,办公室里的猫对公司来说仍是一项巨大的成功。这项政策促使其他多家公司也采取了同样的做法。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the Japanese IT firm?

options.text: It donates money to overpopulated animal shelters.
It permits employees to bring cats into their office.
It gives 5,000 yen to employees who keep pet cats.
It allows workers to do whatever their hearts desire.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Hidenobu Fukuda, who heads the firm, introduced the pet policy, upon request from one of his employees, allowing staff to bring their own cats to work.信号：政策核心句直陈 。这句用 allowing staff to bring their own cats to work 直接点明政策内容"允许员工带猫上班"，是新闻开头交代"政策是什么"的核心陈述句，无需转折，顺听到…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：原文确实提到 shelters，也提到给钱，但给钱的对象是"救猫的员工"而非"收容所"。本项 It donates money to overpopulated animal shelters. 把"给员工"偷换成"给收容所"，盗用了原文 overpopulated shelters 这个词来骗你。 借用原文：He gives 5,000 yen, about 45 US dollars a month to those who rescue a cat
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文的 5,000 yen 是发给"救助了猫的人"，不是发给"养宠物猫的员工"。本项 It gives 5,000 yen to employees who keep pet cats. 照搬了 5,000 yen 这个醒目数字，却把领钱条件从"rescue a cat"换成"keep pet cats"，属听到数字就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：do whatever their little hearts desire
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文 do whatever their little hearts desire 的主语是猫（furry friends），形容猫在办公室自由活动。本项 It allows workers to do whatever their hearts desire. 几乎原句照抄，却把主语从"猫"偷换成"workers（员工）"，是典型原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（allowing staff to bring their own cats to work ↔ It permits employees to bring cats into their office allowing≈permits、staff≈employees）

questions.evidenceText: Hidenobu Fukuda, who heads the firm, introduced the pet policy, upon request from one of his employees, allowing staff to bring their own cats to work.

questions.stem: What does Fukuda encourage his employees to do?

options.text: Volunteer to help in animal shelters.
Contribute to a fund for cat protection.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Not only does Fukuda encourage bringing cats to the job, but he also encourages his employees to rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets.信号：encourages领起的鼓励句 。题干问 encourage 什么，原文里正好两次出现 encourage，answer 落在 he also encourages his employees to 后面跟的动词 …

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：原文说的是把街上的猫"救回来（rescue from streets）"，本项 Keep cats off the street. 借用了"街"这个意象，却说成"让猫别上街"，动作方向正好相反。 借用原文：rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：本项 Volunteer to help in animal shelters. 盗用了原文出现的 shelters，但原文只说"从收容所救猫"，从没说鼓励员工"去收容所做义工"。听到 shelters 就选 C，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：He gives 5,000 yen, about 45 US dollars a month to those who rescue a cat
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：原文是"公司给救猫的员工 5,000 日元"，钱是公司发出去的；本项 Contribute to a fund for cat protection. 却说成"员工往护猫基金捐钱"，把给钱方向倒置，且"基金"原文从未出现。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets ↔ Rescue homeless cats from shelters or streets≈homeless）

questions.evidenceText: Not only does Fukuda encourage bringing cats to the job, but he also encourages his employees to rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the firm's policy?

options.text: It has contributed tremendously to the firm's fame.
It has helped a lot to improve animals' well-being.
It has led some other companies to follow suit.
It has resulted in damage to office equipment.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Still, cats in the workplace have been a tremendous success for the company. The policy has led to various other companies doing the same.信号：结尾Still转折后的总评 。末段以 Still 转折，把前一段的"小麻烦"翻过去，落到对政策的总评"a tremendous success"，紧接 The policy has led to various ot…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：原文只说政策是 a tremendous success（巨大成功），并未说提升了公司"名气"。本项 It has contributed tremendously to the firm's fame. 盗用了 tremendous 这个词，把"成功"擅自推成"出名"，属听到 tremendous 就想选的原词陷阱叠加过度推断。 借用原文：they shut down the computers by walking onto the off switch
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：本项 It has helped a lot to improve animals' well-being. 听着与"救助流浪猫"沾边，但新闻评价政策结果时讲的是"对公司的成功"和"被别家效仿"，并没有评价它"改善了动物福祉"，这句结论原文未提。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文确有猫踩电话、踩关机键的内容，但那被归为 some obstacles（一些小障碍），且被末段 Still 转折掉，并非对政策的总体评价。本项 It has resulted in damage to office equipment. 盗用了"电脑/电话"这段细节冒充总评，属原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The policy has led to various other companies doing the same ↔ It has led some other companies to follow suit doing the same≈follow suit）

questions.evidenceText: Still, cats in the workplace have been a tremendous success for the company. The policy has led to various other companies doing the same.

transcript.text: M: Has Jimmy been coming in lately?
transcript.zh: M: Jimmy 最近有来吗？

transcript.text: W: No, I haven't seen him around. Why? Has he been causing any trouble?
transcript.zh: W: 没有，我没见他在附近。怎么了？他惹什么麻烦了吗？

transcript.text: M: Not that I know of. But I need to see him, because my friends and I lent him some money last month. We haven't heard from him since. I heard he comes here a lot, so I thought I'd come in and check with you.
transcript.zh: M: 据我所知没有。但我需要见他，因为上个月我和朋友们借了他一些钱。从那以后就没他消息了。我听说他经常来这儿，所以想过来问问你。

transcript.text: W: Well, that's funny. Some other fellow came in asking for Jimmy just yesterday, a real nervous, pushy type of fellow, saying he needed Jimmy for some study project they were working on. But I can't quite remember what it was all about. Is this a lot of money we're talking about here?
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，这倒挺有意思。就在昨天还有个人来找 Jimmy，一个特别紧张、咄咄逼人的家伙，说他需要找 Jimmy 完成他们一起做的什么学习项目。但我记不太清具体是什么了。你们说的是一大笔钱吗？

transcript.text: M: No, just 60 pounds between the three of us, but still a bit too much to just let go. He told us he'd got into an accident. Nothing serious, mind you, but he damaged someone's car and wanted to get some money together to make up for the damage he'd caused.
transcript.zh: M: 不是，我们三个人一共就 60 英镑，但也不至于就这么算了。他告诉我们他出了个事故。不严重，你知道，但他撞坏了别人的车，想凑点钱赔偿他造成的损失。

transcript.text: W: Hmm, isn't that sort of thing usually covered by insurance? And then, if you still wanted to give money as some sort of apology or something, he probably shouldn't have to go around borrowing it from people.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，这种事不是通常都有保险赔吗？而且就算你还想给钱作为某种道歉什么的，他也不应该到处找人借钱吧。

transcript.text: M: You think Jimmy's just making it all up? See, I did think it was a bit weird for him to be asking for money for that sort of thing. And his story was a bit vague to begin with. But I thought maybe he doesn't want his parents to know about what happened. So he'd rather come to us and keep things quiet. Anyway, Jimmy is a good guy. So we didn't make a fuss about it.

transcript.text: W: Hi, Max. How are you? Listen. I wanted to ask you about ordering shopping online. I've never done it before and I know that you've been doing it for ages.
transcript.zh: W: 嗨, Max。你好吗?听着,我想问你关于网上购物的事。我以前从来没试过,我知道你已经用了很久了。

transcript.text: M: Sure. I love getting my shopping delivered. It makes life so much simpler—no carrying heavy shopping bags in the rain, or trying to park the car on those huge supermarket car parks then not being able to find it again after you come out of the shops.
transcript.zh: M: 当然。我很喜欢送货上门。这让生活简单多了——不用在雨天提着沉重的购物袋,也不用在那些超大的超市停车场停车,然后从商店出来后又找不到自己的车。

transcript.text: W: But there must be some problems. I mean, how do you know that you won't get bad fruit, or that the eggs won't be broken?
transcript.zh: W: 但肯定会有些问题吧。我是说,你怎么知道不会买到坏水果,或者鸡蛋不会破呢?

transcript.text: M: Oh, come on. The food is exactly the same as the stuff you buy in a conventional shop. They aren't going to deliver you food that is out of date. And if you get a broken egg, well, that could happen in a conventional shop, too. If anything is really wrong, you can just take photographs of the damage, and they will give you the money back or replace the item.
transcript.zh: M: 哦,别这样。食物和你在传统商店买的东西完全一样。他们不会给你送过期的食品。如果你收到破损的鸡蛋,这在传统商店也可能发生。如果真的有什么问题,你可以拍下损坏的照片,他们会退钱或者换货。

transcript.text: W: How about delivery fees? Is it not more expensive to get everything delivered?
transcript.zh: W: 配送费怎么样?送货上门不是更贵吗?

transcript.text: M: I actually found that it was cheaper for me, as I live quite far away from my local supermarket. So with the deliveries, I'm actually saving on petrol.
transcript.zh: M: 实际上我发现对我来说更便宜,因为我住得离本地超市挺远的。所以有了配送服务,我实际上还节省了汽油费。

transcript.text: W: I've never thought of that. If you aren't driving your own car, then you are saving on fuel. Right, you've convinced me. I'm going to go on the computer now and give it a try. So, which supermarket do you think is the best to order from?
transcript.zh: W: 我从没想过这一点。如果你不开自己的车,那就省了油钱。好吧,你说服我了。我现在就去电脑上试试。那么,你觉得哪家超市最值得下单?

transcript.text: M: Oh, no. That's definitely up to you. Otherwise, we'll be here all day.
transcript.zh: M: 哦,不。那肯定要你自己决定。否则,我们得在这儿待一整天了。

transcript.text: A recent study found that 10 percent of British children suffer from math anxiety. This means they have overwhelming negative emotions towards the subject, ranging from rage to despair. Other emotions triggered by math include feelings of "tension and frustration". Physical symptoms include a racing heart or struggling to catch breath.
transcript.zh: 最近一项研究发现,10%的英国儿童患有数学焦虑症。这意味着他们对这门学科有压倒性的负面情绪,从愤怒到绝望不等。数学引发的其他情绪还包括"紧张和挫败感"。生理症状包括心跳加速或呼吸困难。

transcript.text: The phenomenon of math anxiety is characterized as a general sense of feeling that the subject is hard compared with other subjects leading to a subsequent lack or loss of confidence.
transcript.zh: 数学焦虑现象的特征是一种普遍的感觉,即认为这门学科比其他学科更难,从而导致信心不足或丧失信心。

transcript.text: Researchers said they investigated individuals' attitudes towards mathematics because of what could be referred to as a mathematics crisis in the UK. There's a widespread misunderstanding that only low performing children suffer from math anxiety. People automatically assume children are anxious about math because they are poor achievers.
transcript.zh: 研究人员表示,他们之所以调查个人对数学的态度,是因为英国可以称之为数学危机的现象。人们普遍误解只有成绩差的儿童才会患有数学焦虑症。人们自动认为儿童对数学感到焦虑是因为他们成绩不好。

transcript.text: In fact, more than three quarters of children with high levels of math anxiety are normal to high achievers.
transcript.zh: 事实上,超过四分之三有高度数学焦虑的儿童是正常到高水平的成就者。

transcript.text: Probably their math anxiety will go unnoticed because their performance is good. But in the long term their performance is negatively affected.
transcript.zh: 他们的数学焦虑可能不会被注意到,因为他们的成绩很好。但从长远来看,他们的表现会受到负面影响。

transcript.text: So the real danger here is that children who will be completely able to do math at a normal level may keep away from it because they feel anxious.
transcript.zh: 所以真正的危险在于,完全有能力达到正常水平做数学的儿童可能会远离它,因为他们感到焦虑。

transcript.text: Math anxiety can severely disrupt students' performance in the subject in both primary and secondary school. But importantly—and surprisingly—this new study suggests that the majority of students experiencing math anxiety have normal to high math ability.
transcript.zh: 数学焦虑会严重扰乱学生在小学和中学阶段这门学科的表现。但重要的是——也令人惊讶的是——这项新研究表明,大多数经历数学焦虑的学生具有正常到较高的数学能力。

options.text: They have little talent for learning math.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A recent study found that 10 percent of British children suffer from math anxiety. This means they have overwhelming negative emotions towards the subject, ranging from rage to despair.信号：found 后接结论加 This means 解释 。信号有两层：先是 A recent study found that 直接打出「研究发现」的旗号，这后面就是答案区；紧接着 This means they hav…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：little talent for learning math 借了话题词 math 来制造熟悉感，但录音通篇讲的是「情绪」，从没说这些孩子「缺乏天赋」——恰恰相反，后文还强调他们能力中上。这是把「焦虑」想当然地等同于「没天赋」的常识误判。 借用原文：a racing heart or struggling to catch breath
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：medical help for math anxiety 原样搬来录音的 math anxiety，又把后文的身体症状 a racing heart or struggling to catch breath 误读成「需要医疗帮助」。但录音只是描述症状，从没说这些孩子需要看病求医，属于借原词、推过头。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：extra help to catch up in the math class 蹭了 math 这个话题，但「需要额外帮助跟上数学课」在录音里完全没有对应——录音讲的是情绪，不是学业进度落后。属于无中生有的干扰。

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：There's a widespread misunderstanding that only low performing children suffer from math anxiety. People automatically assume children are anxious about math because they are poor achievers.信号：widespread misunderstanding that 直接引出误解内容 。信号词是 a widespread misunderstanding that——它和题干用词几乎一模一样，that 后面那句就是…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It will gradually pass away without teachers' help. 说焦虑会在没有老师帮助下自行消退——录音从没这么说，反而强调 in the long term their performance is negatively affected（长期看会损害成绩）。属于录音没提、且与原意相悖的编造。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：It is related to a child's low intelligence. 借了录音 low performing 里的 low，把「成绩差（low performing / poor achievers）」偷换成了「智力低（low intelligence）」。录音谈的是学业表现，从没说焦虑跟智商有关，是典型的偷换概念。 借用原文：they are poor achievers

optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（only low performing children suffer from math anxiety ↔ It affects low performing children only suffer from 换成 affects，主被动对调）

questions.stem: What does the passage say about British students with math anxiety?

options.text: Most of them have average to strong math ability.
Most of them get timely help from their teachers.
They will regain confidence with counselling.
They are mostly secondary school students.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：But importantly—and surprisingly—this new study suggests that the majority of students experiencing math anxiety have normal to high math ability.信号：But 加 importantly 加 surprisingly 三重强调收尾 。信号极强：But importantly—and surprisingly 同时用了转折 but、强调 importantly、反直觉…

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：Most of them get timely help from their teachers. 录音恰恰相反：their math anxiety will go unnoticed because their performance is good——因为成绩好，焦虑往往被忽视、得不到关注，谈何「及时得到老师帮助」。这是与原文相反的干扰。 借用原文：both primary and secondary school
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：They will regain confidence with counselling. 里的 counselling（心理咨询）在录音里从头到尾没出现过，「靠咨询恢复信心」完全是编造。录音只提到 a subsequent lack or loss of confidence（信心丧失），但从没说怎么靠咨询找回。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：They are mostly secondary school students. 借了录音 in both primary and secondary school 里的 secondary school，却偷偷把「小学和中学都有」缩成「主要是中学生」。录音明说两个学段都受影响，选项却用 mostly 把范围卡死，属范围偷改。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the majority of students experiencing math anxiety ↔ Most of them the majority of=Most of）

transcript.text: People spend a lot of time using phones and computers. Much of that time is devoted to text messages and social media. But many people choose to spend their time playing computer games.
transcript.zh: 人们花费大量时间使用手机和电脑。这些时间大部分用于发送短信和使用社交媒体。但许多人选择把时间花在玩电脑游戏上。

transcript.text: For years, parents and teachers have worried that these games might be addictive. And now, the World Health Organization has recognized addiction to computer games as a disease. The organization explains that this decision reflects general agreement among experts around the world that some people have a problem with these games. They show a pattern of behavior characterized by a lack of control. Such people make computer games a priority over their responsibilities. They may play games instead of attending school, or work, or socializing.
transcript.zh: 多年来,家长和教师一直担心这些游戏可能会让人上瘾。现在,世界卫生组织已经将电脑游戏成瘾认定为一种疾病。该组织解释说,这一决定反映了全球专家的普遍共识,即有些人在这些游戏上存在问题。他们表现出以缺乏控制力为特征的行为模式。这些人将电脑游戏置于自己的责任之上。他们可能不去上学、不去工作或不参加社交活动,而是玩游戏。

transcript.text: According to the World Health Organization experts, people's use of computer games is different from their use of the Internet, social media and online shopping. These experts claim there is not sufficient data to indicate that people's reliance on those other activities is an addiction. But they argue that playing computer games to access is different. This behavior can become a disorder. To meet the new definition for addiction, the behavior must damage a person's relationships or performance at school or work, and this must last for at least a year. Still not all behavior experts agree. Some argue that there's not enough research on the subject. Thus, they claim it is too early to call computer game addiction a disorder.
transcript.zh: 根据世界卫生组织专家的说法,人们对电脑游戏的使用不同于他们对互联网、社交媒体和网上购物的使用。这些专家声称,没有足够的数据表明人们对其他这些活动的依赖是一种成瘾。但他们认为,为了获取而玩电脑游戏是不同的。这种行为可能成为一种障碍。要符合成瘾的新定义,这种行为必须损害一个人的人际关系或在学校或工作中的表现,并且这种情况必须持续至少一年。但并非所有行为专家都同意这一观点。一些人认为关于这个主题的研究还不够充分。因此,他们声称现在将电脑游戏成瘾称为一种障碍还为时过早。

questions.stem: What conclusion has the World Health Organization come to recently?

options.text: Social media addiction is a threat to our health.
Too many people are addicted to smartphones.
Addiction to computer games is a disease.
Computer games can be rather addictive.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：And now, the World Health Organization has recognized addiction to computer games as a disease.信号：主语复现 + now 标志新结论 。录音里 And now, the World Health Organization has recognized addiction to computer games as a…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音第 1 段确实提到 social media、第 2 段提到这是健康相关的话题，A 就把"social media"和"health"拼成"社交媒体成瘾威胁健康"，但 WHO 下结论的对象是电子游戏成瘾、不是社交媒体，听到熟词就选会掉进这个坑。 借用原文：People spend a lot of time using phones and computers.
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音开头说 People spend a lot of time using phones and computers.，B 就顺势说"太多人沉迷智能手机"，可录音的结论针对的是"游戏成瘾"而非"手机成瘾"，且"太多人"是它没下过的数量判断，属于借原词制造的干扰。 借用原文：these games might be addictive
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D Computer games can be rather addictive. 只是说游戏"挺容易让人上瘾"，这是第 2 段开头家长老师的担忧口吻 these games might be addictive，远没到 WHO"认定为疾病"的硬定性；问的是 WHO 的结论，就必须取那句最重的定性，故 D 程度偏轻、被排除。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（recognized addiction to computer games as a disease ↔ Addiction to computer games is a disease. "认定…为疾病"="…是疾病"）

questions.evidenceText: And now, the World Health Organization has recognized addiction to computer games as a disease.

questions.stem: What is said of people with addictive behavior?

options.text: They prioritize their favored activity over what they should do.
They do their favored activity whenever and wherever possible.
They are unaware of the damage their behavior is doing to them.
They are unable to get rid of their addiction without professional help.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Such people make computer games a priority over their responsibilities.信号：指示词"Such people"领起对该类人的刻画 。录音用 Such people make computer games a priority over their responsibilities. 中的"Su…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B They do their favored activity whenever and wherever possible. 说成瘾者"随时随地都玩"，但录音从头到尾没说过"whenever and wherever（任何时间任何地点）"，它只说这些人拿游戏顶替了上学、工作、社交 They may play games instead of attending school, or work, or socializing.，"随时随地"是凭常识脑补出来的。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C They are unaware of the damage their behavior is doing to them. 说成瘾者"意识不到自己受的伤害"，录音确实提到这种行为会 damage a person's relationships or performance（损害关系或表现），但只说"有危害"，从没说成瘾者"没意识到"，C 把"有危害"偷换成了"本人不自知"。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D They are unable to get rid of their addiction without professional help. 说成瘾者"离了专业帮助戒不掉"，录音通篇在讨论"算不算病"，从未提及"professional help（专业帮助）"或"戒不掉"，这是套用对"成瘾"的刻板印象添加的内容。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（make computer games a priority over their responsibilities ↔ They prioritize their favored activity over what they should do. "把游戏看得比责任重"="把爱做的事置于该做的事之上"）

questions.evidenceText: Such people make computer games a priority over their responsibilities.

questions.stem: What do some behavior experts think of addiction to computer games?

options.text: It may be less damaging than previously believed.
There will never be agreement on its harm to people.
It may prove to be beneficial to developing creativity.
There is not enough evidence to classify it as a disease.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P3）：Still not all behavior experts agree. Some argue that there's not enough research on the subject. Thus, they claim it is too early to call computer game addiction a disorder.信号：转折词 Still 领出反对声音 。录音用 Still not all behavior experts agree. 中的"Still"（不过、然而）把语气从前文 WHO 的定论转向反方，紧接着的 Some arg…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A It may be less damaging than previously believed. 说"危害可能比以前认为的小"，录音里反方专家质疑的是"研究够不够、能不能现在就定性"，从没比较过"危害大小"，damaging 一词虽在第 3 段出现过 damage a person's relationships，但"less damaging（危害更小）"是录音没有的比较。 借用原文：Still not all behavior experts agree.
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：B There will never be agreement on its harm to people. 说"永远不会就其危害达成一致"，录音只说现在"not all…agree（并非都同意）"、还需要更多研究，是"暂时未达成一致"，绝不是"永远不会一致"，never 把话推到了录音没有的极端。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C It may prove to be beneficial to developing creativity. 说游戏成瘾"可能有益于培养创造力"，录音通篇在争论"算不算病"，从未出现 beneficial（有益）或 creativity（创造力）任何相关内容，这是凭空添加的好处。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（there's not enough research on the subject ↔ There is not enough evidence to classify it as a disease. "研究不够"="证据不足以定性为疾病"）

questions.evidenceText: Still not all behavior experts agree. Some argue that there's not enough research on the subject. Thus, they claim it is too early to call computer game addiction a disorder.

transcript.text: Maybe you carry the most powerful passport in the world, or perhaps the rarest passport. Whatever the case, your passport will likely be one of four colors: red, blue, green or black, although there are slight variations. Switzerland's passport is dark red, for example, while most European countries prefer a shade of red. That's almost brown.
transcript.zh: 也许你持有世界上最强大的护照,或者可能是最稀有的护照。无论如何,你的护照很可能是四种颜色之一:红色、蓝色、绿色或黑色,尽管存在细微的差异。例如,瑞士的护照是深红色,而大多数欧洲国家更喜欢红色的色调。那几乎是棕色的。

transcript.text: There are no official rules regarding passport colors, but countries follow a certain set of norms when designing them. The International Civil Aviation Organization, which works to define the principles of air travel, suggests that countries use a suitable type, size and style for official documents like passports.
transcript.zh: 关于护照颜色没有官方规定,但各国在设计护照时遵循一套特定的规范。国际民用航空组织致力于定义航空旅行的原则,建议各国为护照等官方文件使用合适的类型、尺寸和样式。

transcript.text: There are also a few compulsory aspects of passports. They must be made from a material that bends. They should be able to be read by a machine at temperatures ranging from 10 degrees Celsius to 50 degrees Celsius, under the conditions where the air can be extremely dry or moist.
transcript.zh: 护照还有一些强制性要求。护照必须由可弯曲的材料制成。它们应当能够在10摄氏度到50摄氏度的温度范围内被机器读取,在空气可能极度干燥或潮湿的条件下。

transcript.text: Despite these existing recommendations, there is nothing regarding the cover color. Why? Simply put, countries stick to darker and more conservative colors because they appear more official. And they can also hide dirt and wear. While there's little innovation when it comes to passport cover color, the same cannot be said for the pages. The passports of many countries can take images of their well-known geographical features and wildlife, which also function as security features as some are only visible under a special light.
transcript.zh: 尽管存在这些现行建议,但没有关于封面颜色的规定。为什么?简单来说,各国坚持使用更深、更保守的颜色,因为它们看起来更正式。而且它们还可以隐藏污垢和磨损。虽然在护照封面颜色方面几乎没有创新,但在内页方面却并非如此。许多国家的护照可以采用其著名地理特征和野生动物的图像,这些图像也具有安全功能,因为有些图像只有在特殊光线下才能看到。

questions.stem: What do we learn about most European passports?

options.text: They are relatively uniform in color and design.
They appear more formal than other passports.
They are a shade of red bordering on brown.
They vary in color from country to country.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Switzerland's passport is dark red, for example, while most European countries prefer a shade of red. That's almost brown.信号：听到题干对象就锁定 。录音念到 most European countries prefer a shade of red，正好对应题干的 most European passports，这就是答案句的信号——题干问…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：relatively uniform in color and design 借了原文反复出现的 color、design 话题词制造熟悉感，但录音说欧洲护照偏爱某种红色，并未说各国颜色与设计相对统一，属于听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：they appear more official
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：more formal than other passports 把后文第 4 段讲深色封面显得正式 they appear more official 张冠李戴到欧洲护照颜色这题上，且 formal 与 official 近义诱人，但本题问的是欧洲护照颜色，不是封面为何显正式。 借用原文：most European countries prefer a shade of red
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：vary in color from country to country 与录音相反——录音强调 most European countries prefer a shade of red，即多数欧洲国家偏爱同一种红色，是趋同而非各国不同，选项把意思反了。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（most European countries prefer a shade of red ↔ They are a shade of red bordering on brown. 原话原词搬进选项）

questions.evidenceText: Switzerland's passport is dark red, for example, while most European countries prefer a shade of red. That's almost brown.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the design of passports?

options.text: They must endure wear and tear.
They must be of the same size.
They must be made from a rare material.
They must follow some common standards.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：There are no official rules regarding passport colors, but countries follow a certain set of norms when designing them.信号：转折 but 后是真意 。There are no official rules 先说没有官方规定，but 之后才转到 countries follow a certain set of norms when des…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：endure wear and tear 里的磨损来自第 4 段 hide dirt and wear，录音确实念过 wear，但那是讲深色封面能藏脏污磨损，不是回答护照设计要遵守什么，听到 wear 就选即落入原词陷阱。 借用原文：size
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：of the same size 看似与第 2 段 size 沾边，但录音只说建议各国采用合适的类型、尺寸与样式，从未说护照必须大小相同，属借 size 一词的原词陷阱兼未提及。 借用原文：made from a material that bends
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：made from a rare material 借了第 3 段 made from a material 的 material 一词，但录音只要求材料能弯折，从未说稀有，rare 是凭空加上去的，属原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（follow a certain set of norms ↔ follow some common standards norms 与 standards 同义）

questions.evidenceText: There are no official rules regarding passport colors, but countries follow a certain set of norms when designing them.

questions.stem: Why are dark colors chosen for passport covers?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Simply put, countries stick to darker and more conservative colors because they appear more official.信号：because 引出原因 。录音 Simply put 提示要给结论，紧接 because they appear more official 用 because 直接交代原因——这正是 Why 题的答案信号，bec…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：look more traditional 与正确项 look more official 仅一词之差，traditional（传统）与 official（官方）近义易混，但录音 because 后说的是 more official，从未说 traditional，命题人就靠这对近义词诱你听岔。 借用原文：The International Civil Aviation Organization
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：favored by airlines 蹭了第 2 段提到的国际民航组织 The International Civil Aviation Organization 这一航空背景，但录音从没说深色封面受航空公司青睐，把民航组织硬扯成 airlines 偏好，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：hide dirt and wear
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：easily identifiable 是另起的一个特征，录音讲深色封面的原因是显官方、还能藏脏污磨损 hide dirt and wear，从未说深色是为了易于辨识，与本题原因不符，属答非所问。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（they appear more official ↔ They look more official. appear 与 look 同义）

questions.evidenceText: Simply put, countries stick to darker and more conservative colors because they appear more official.

questions.stem: What is one special function of the images inside many passports?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：The passports of many countries can take images of their well-known geographical features and wildlife, which also function as security features as some are only visible under a special light.信号：function as 点出作用 。录音 which also function as security features 用 function as 直接点明图案的作用是安全防伪——这正是问 function 一题…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：For beauty. 看似与内页印著名地理风貌、野生动物图案 images of their well-known geographical features and wildlife 沾边，会让人觉得图案是为好看，但录音说的功能是安全防伪，从未说为了美观，属过度推断兼未提及。 借用原文：the same cannot be said for the pages
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：For variety. 蹭了录音讲各国内页图案不同、内页比封面有变化这层意思 the same cannot be said for the pages，但那是说内页设计较多样，不是图案的功能，把内页多样性误当成图案功能，属答非所问。 借用原文：only visible under a special light
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：For visibility. 直接盗用录音 only visible under a special light 里的 visible 一词，且与正确项 For security 拼写相近极易混，但原文说的是图案只在特殊光下可见、这恰恰服务于安全防伪，可见只是手段、安全才是功能，听到 visible 就选即落入原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（function as security features ↔ For security. security 原词即功能）

He is now supporting " 32______ benches," which are public seating areas where people are encouraged to go and chat with one another. The minister is also 33______ to stop public transportation from being cut in ways that leave people isolated.

More than one-fifth of adults in both the United States and Britain said in a 2018 34______ that they often or always feel lonely. paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Numbers do not exist in all cultures. There are numberless hunter-gatherers in Amazonia, living along branches of the world's largest river tree. Instead of using words for precise quantities, these people rely exclusively on terms similar to "a few" or "some." In contrast, our own lives are governed by numbers. As you read this, you are likely aware of what time it is, how old you are, your checking account balance, your weight and so on. The exact numbers we think with impact everything in our lives.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: But, in a historical sense, number-conscious people like us are the unusual ones. For the bulk of our species' approximately 200,000-year lifespan, we had no means of precisely representing quantities. What's more, the 7,000 or so languages that exist today vary dramatically in how they utilize numbers.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Speakers of anumeric, or numberless, languages offer a window into how the invention of numbers reshaped the human experience. Cultures without numbers, or with only one or two precise numbers, include the Munduruku and Piraha in Amazonia. Researchers have also studied some adults in Nicaragua who were never taught number words. Without numbers, healthy human adults struggle to precisely distinguish and recall quantities as low as four. In an experiment, a researcher will place nuts into a can one at a time and then remove them one by one. The person watching is asked to signal when all the nuts have been removed. Responses suggest that anumeric people have some trouble keeping track of how many nuts remain in the can, even if there are only four or five in total.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: This and many other experiments have led to a simple conclusion: When people do not have number words, they struggle to make quantitative distinctions that probably seem natural to someone like you or me. While only a small portion of the world's languages are anumeric or nearly anumeric, they demonstrate that number words are not a human universal.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: It is worth stressing that these anumeric people are cognitively(在认知方面) normal, well-adapted to the surroundings they have dominated for centuries. As a child, I spent some time living with anumeric people, the Piraha who live along the banks of the black Maici River. Like other outsiders, I was continually impressed by their superior understanding of the ecology we shared. Yet numberless people struggle with tasks that require precise discrimination between quantities. Perhaps this should be unsurprising. After all, without counting, how can someone tell whether there are, say, seven or eight coconuts(椰子) in a tree? Such seemingly straightforward distinctions become blurry through numberless eyes.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: This conclusion is echoed by work with anumeric children in industrialized societies. Prior to being spoon-fed number words, children can only approximately discriminate quantities beyond three. We must be handed the cognitive tools of numbers before we can consistently and easily recognize higher quantities. In fact, acquiring the exact meaning of number words is a painstaking process that takes children years. Initially, kids learn numbers much like they learn letters. They recognize that numbers are organized sequentially, but have little awareness of what each individual number means. With time, they start to understand that a given number represents a quantity greater by one than the number coming before it. This "successor principle" is part of the foundation of our numerical(数字的) cognition, but requires extensive practice to understand.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: None of us, then, is really a "numbers person." We are not born to handle quantitative distinctions skillfully. In the absence of the cultural traditions that fill our lives with numbers from infancy, we would all struggle with even basic quantitative distinctions. Number words and their written forms transform our quantitative reasoning as they are introduced into our cognitive experience by our parents, peers and school teachers. The process seems so normal that we sometimes think of it as a natural part of growing up, but it is not. Human brains come equipped with certain quantitative instincts that are refined with age, but these instincts are very limited.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Compared with other mammals, our numerical instincts are not as remarkable as many assume. We even share some basic instinctual quantitative reasoning with distant non-mammalian relatives like birds. Indeed, work with some other species suggests they too can refine their quantitative thought if they are introduced to the cognitive power tools we call numbers.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: So, how did we ever invent "unnatural" numbers in the first place? The answer is, literally, at your fingertips. The bulk of the world's languages use base-10, base-20 or base-5 number systems. That is, these smaller numbers are the basis of larger numbers. English is a base-10 or decimal(十进制的) language, as evidenced by words like 14("four" + "10") and 31 ("three" x "10" + "one"). We speak a decimal language because an ancestral tongue, proto-Indo-European, was decimally based. Proto-Indo-European was decimally oriented because, as in so many cultures, our ancestors' hands served as the gateway to the realization that "five fingers on one hand is the same as five fingers on the other." Such momentary thoughts were represented in words and passed down across generations. This is why the word "five" in many languages is derived from the word for "hand." Most number systems, then, are the by-product of two key factors: the human capacity for language and our inclination for focusing on our hands and fingers. This manual fixation—an indirect by-product of walking upright on two legs—has helped yield numbers in most cultures, but not all.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Cultures without numbers also offer insight into the cognitive influence of particular numeric traditions. Consider what time it is. Your day is ruled by minutes and seconds, but these concepts are not real in any physical sense and are nonexistent to numberless people. Minutes and seconds are the verbal and written representations of an uncommon base-60 number system used in ancient Mesopotamia. They reside in our minds, numerical artifacts(人工制品) that not all humans inherit conceptually.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Research on the language of numbers shows, more and more, that one of our species' key characteristics is tremendous linguistic(语言的) and cognitive diversity. If we are to truly understand how much our cognitive lives differ cross-culturally, we must continually explore the depths of our species' linguistic diversity.
